Equal block sums force an affine arithmetic progression of centered endpoint sums; nonzero slope is bounded by discrepancy, and zero slope contradicts nonconstant F_r on a nonzero endpoint residue. Direct q-aligned blocks prove the complementary existence. The executable finite checks passed, but the symbolic proof is essential.

originality.rationale: The 2024 additive-complexity paper classifies ternary generalized Thue-Morse factor-sum diversity and investigates Tribonacci power orders, not an all-base fixed-order unbounded-exponent classification. Chen–Wen computes abelian complexity and boundary vectors, not the simultaneous equal-sum condition across arbitrarily many length-ell blocks. Ordinary critical-exponent literature concerns strictly equal words. Targeted published-record and primary-source comparisons found no dominating result; unpublished/unindexed work remains possible.

value.rationale: Complete natural classification over all generalized Thue–Morse alphabets and fixed block lengths, in a notion explicitly motivated by the 2024 source. Arbitrarily large additive exponents globally are known from bounded additive complexity, but deciding their possibility at an arbitrarily prescribed fixed order is structurally different. The effective arithmetic-phase lemma gives meaningful uniform impossibility over starts; neither sharp excluded exponents nor a paper-length result is claimed.
